curriculum: The 2026–2027 guide distinguishes the standard Computer Science BSc from the open bachelor and Information Science. It confirms 12 compulsory 5 EC foundation courses, 15 compulsory 5 EC advanced taught courses, a 15 EC graduation project and 30 EC of free electives. The curriculum totals 180 EC and is Dutch-taught, part-time and paced flexibly. The official learning lines are software technology, information systems and communication technology.
progression: The guide provides September and February suggested part-time schedules with variable and fixed starts. Introductory programming supports advanced object-oriented work; the foundation practicum draws on programming, design and databases. Networks and algorithms prepare operating systems, and AppLab integrates upper computing work. Graduation Project Preparation (IB9902) requires the foundation plus at least twelve specified advanced courses, including the starred courses. The current project page confirms the remaining courses, including preparation and free electives, must be passed, credited or already being studied under the online study plan unless the examiner permits entry. The project involves supervised research with a thesis and presentation. The comparator comparison is organised by curriculum rather than imposing UCR semesters on OU.
